creator: adam_ha_yes
title: Designer's 'vibe coder evolution' ladder: study product structure and Laws of UX -> Bolt/Lovable -> Mobbin/Pinterest references -> Claude Code CLI -> Codex for full features -> Ghostty with 6 terminals + GitHub

tools.name: Laws of UX
tools.detail: '21+ laws', read all of them to understand grouping and aesthetics-for-conversion

tools.name: Mobbin
tools.detail: Design reference library ('Mobin design'); use screens as reference images

tools.name: Pinterest
tools.detail: Find designs you like, use as reference images

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.detail: CLI; 'create an iOS app for you in this folder', run in Xcode; creator still uses it for most front-end

tools.name: Codex (CLI)
tools.detail: Creator says currently better than Claude at full features

tools.name: Ghostty
tools.detail: Terminal app; runs up to 6 terminals with Codex and Claude Code side by side

tools.name: GitHub
tools.detail: Push to origin main or branches, test locally

claims: Creator has spent 'tens of thousands of dollars' on Claude Code and Codex
Started as a UI/UX product designer, now ships full-stack features without knowing how to code
'Right now Codex is actually a lot better at full features than Claude'; Claude still used for most front-end
Runs up to 6 terminals at once doing different operations
Vibe coding is 'pretty cheap right now and might be more expensive in the future'
how_to_steps: Study how everyday products (LinkedIn, X, TikTok) are structured and why UI elements are where they are
Start with Bolt or Lovable by describing an app (e.g. 'a meditation app')
Layer in taste: pull references from Mobbin or Pinterest and feed them as reference images
Move to Claude Code CLI in the terminal; ask it to scaffold an iOS app in a folder and run it in Xcode
Add Codex CLI for full features; keep Claude for front-end
Use Ghostty with multiple terminals (up to 6) running Codex and Claude Code in parallel
Connect the project to GitHub; push to main/branches, test locally
on_screen_only: Caption overlay throughout: 'The evolution of a "vibe coder"'
One frame shows a mobile app design board (Figma/Mobbin-style grid of phone screens: red logo splash, product photos, color swatches, 'Onboarding' notes) -- no readable text

relevance.why: Beginner ladder; Haji is already at the top rung (Claude Code daily). Only the design-taste inputs (Laws of UX, Mobbin) and the Ghostty multi-terminal habit are usable nuggets.

implement_score.why: Bookmark Mobbin + Laws of UX as reference sources to feed Claude Design / Claude Code when building UI; optional: try Ghostty for parallel Claude Code + Codex panes. An hour, no money.

verify: Is Mobbin free enough to be useful (it is largely paid)?
Creator's 'Codex better at full features' is a point-in-time opinion -- re-check against current Claude Fable 5 / Opus 5.5
Ghostty: macOS/Linux only; confirm it adds anything over tmux/iTerm splits for Haji

gap.what: Minor: names Mobbin and Laws of UX as taste inputs for vibe-coded UI (liked set covers design skills like Impeccable/Taste but not these reference libraries) and the Ghostty multi-terminal parallel-agent habit.
